correctness.rationale: Connected simple bipartite graphs with p,a guilds and one degree-preserving 2×2 checkerboard switch are ranked by exact NODF (equal-degree pairs score zero) and unrestricted optimum of ordinary Newman–Girvan modularity Q*. A guild size≤2 forces fixed NODF under degree-preserving swaps, reducing n≤7 to 3×3 and 3×4. Independent exhaustive bitmask enumeration checked all connected labeled matrices: 3×3 had 205 graphs, 216 directed connected swaps and 0 co-improvements; 3×4 had 1,795 graphs, 4,320 swaps, 0 co-improvements and 576 strictly opposed changes. A separate complete least-vertex-block DP computes global modularity over all partitions. For the actual two 3×5 witness matrices, independently checked NODF values 5/13 and 11/26 and integer modularity numerators 72 and 78 out of 256 (Q*=9/32,39/128), giving simultaneous strict +1/26 and +3/128. Proof covers the stated finite universal lower bound and witness, not arbitrary larger graphs.
residual_risks: NODF follows exact unequal-degree-pair rule; Q* is unipartite Newman–Girvan optimized over all vertex partitions, NOT Barber bipartite modularity.
The independent finite code used bitmask connected graph enumeration and explicit DP, not just saved verification logs; independent ecological metric conventions can alter the threshold.

value.rationale: At fixed labeled species degrees a degree-preserving local swap isolates structural from degree-sequence effects, while exact global Newman–Girvan optimization avoids heuristic community choices. The sharp connected 8-species onset of simultaneous NODF/modularity increase is a motivated first finite boundary and counterexample with an exact witness, useful as a benchmark for ecological network null models.
residual_risks: Metric normalization and modularity version are essential; not evidence of empirical ecological stability or causal rewiring benefit.
